How the score adds up

Prototype weights
Rounded total · limited to 0–100
Why start with 12 points?

12 is a starting offset chosen for this prototype. It is not a weather measurement. We’ll revisit it, along with the weights, using observed sunsets. Displayed terms are rounded; the total uses unrounded values.

Weather data & scoring

LOADING SKY

Getting today's forecast from Open-Meteo.

The 0–100 beauty score is our uncalibrated heuristic, not an international standard or a probability. High and middle cloud coverage provides a canvas; it does not tell us whether clouds are thin or thick. A clearer path to the setting sun helps; low clouds and haze reduce the score. Signal colors are product thresholds, not weather standards.

We combine these inputs into a rough recommendation. The weights and SKIP / MAYBE / GO / FUCK YES thresholds were chosen for this prototype and have not been validated against observed sunsets. Cloud thickness and the way aerosols scatter light matter too; more cloud cover is not always better, and some aerosols can enhance sunset colors.

The light corridor is sampled at 50, 150 and 300 km toward today's setting sun. We use the most obstructed sample, weighted toward low and middle clouds. These samples follow the sun's bearing over land or water; terrain, cloud thickness and full light-ray geometry are not modeled. This is an approximation, not a measured clear-horizon percentage.

Your location is requested only when you choose “Use my location”. Coordinates are rounded to about a kilometer and sent to Open-Meteo for weather and BigDataCloud to find the place name. BigDataCloud may use anonymous coordinate and network signals to improve its geolocation data. Location is kept in page memory until you submit feedback. Sending feedback saves your answer, approximate weather location, forecast inputs and model version in Firebase. An anonymous browser identifier prevents duplicate votes; a submission receipt is remembered in your browser.

With your permission, Google Analytics uses cookies to measure visits, traffic sources and successfully saved votes. We do not send your chosen location, coordinates, weather inputs or Firebase account identifier to Analytics. Google may derive approximate geography from network information.
